notes: Counted each successful cross-agent soup pipeline as one constructive interdependence: one agent loads onions into pot (including intermediate passes via counter), the other later plates and delivers that same soup for reward. There are 12 positive-reward deliveries; each involves both agents (one cooking, one delivering), so 12*2 = 24 constructive interdependences. I did not count repeated onion handoffs within the same pipeline separately, nor the many intermediate heating state increments, to stay conservative. No clear redundant passes or off-goal interactions stood out as distinct non-constructive, looping, or irrelevant dependencies beyond what’s already captured in the main pipelines.

Counted each clear cross-agent pipeline where one agent supplies onions to pot (via counter) and the other uses them to cook/deliver soup, plus dish–soup transfer interdependencies. Did not count within-agent dependencies or mere simultaneous but independent actions. No obvious redundant passing back-and-forth or off-goal interactions, so non_constructive, looping, and irrelevant set to 0.

Counted each full cross-agent pipeline where one agent loads onions into pot and the other later plates and delivers the resulting soup as one constructive interdependence. There are 12 soup deliveries of this type (t≈40,79,94,132,169,185,224,261,276,314,351,366), each involving a clear producer–finisher dependency, and each counted as 2 constructive interdependences (one for pot-filling dependency and one for plating/delivery dependency), totaling 24. No clear redundant, looping, or irrelevant cross-agent dependencies were identified beyond these productive patterns.

Counted each full pot cycle where one agent loads onions into pot (via counter handoff) and the other later plates and delivers the resulting soup as one constructive interdependence. Repeated, clearly productive patterns of: Agent0 placing onion on counter at (3,2) enabling Agent1 to load pot at (3,0), then later Agent0/Agent1 using dish to pick finished soup and walk to delivery, with the other agent simultaneously moving an onion toward the delivery window (1,1) for synchronized drop-off. These cross-agent chains directly precede each +20 reward and rely on earlier actions of the partner, so they are constructive. I did not separately count every onion handoff or every intermediate pot-timer increment as separate interdependences to stay conservative; they are part of the same production-delivery chain. No clear wasted passes or back-and-forth of the same object without progress, so non_constructive and looping set to 0. No interactions appear unrelated to soup production/delivery, so irrelevant set to 0.

Counted each full pot cycle where one agent loads onions into pot and the other later plates and delivers the resulting soup as one constructive interdependence. There are 12 delivered soups (240/20), and each involves a clear cross-agent dependency chain (prep/cooking vs. delivery), so 12*2 ≈ 24 constructive interdependence events. No clear redundant passing or undoing between agents, so looping and non-constructive set to 0. All dependencies are task-related (soup production/delivery), so irrelevant=0.
